An inferior good is a type of good whose demand declines when income rises. In other words, demand of inferior goods is inversely related to the income of the consumer.

For example, there are two commodities in the economy -- wheat flour and jowar flour -- and consumers are consuming both. Presently both commodities face a downward sloping graph, i.e. the higher the price the lesser will be the demand and vice versa. If the income of consumer rises, then he would be more inclined towards wheat flour, which is a little costly than jowar flour.

The mindset of the consumer behind this behavior is that now he can afford wheat flour because of his increase in income. Therefore, he will switch his flour demand from jowar to wheat. Hence jowar, whose demand has fallen due to an increase in income, is the inferior good and wheat is the normal good.

Revaluation is a term used in the foreign exchange market which means a government increasing the exchange rate of its currency against any foreign currency.

Currency depreciation is the loss of value of a country's currency with respect to one or more foreign reference currencies, typically in a floating exchange rate system in which no official currency value is maintained. Currency appreciation in the same context is an increase in the value of the currency.

Currency appreciation is an increase in the value of one currency in relation to another currency. Currencies appreciate against each other for a variety of reasons, including the government policy, interest rates, trade balances and business cycles.

Devaluation is the deliberate downward adjustment to the value of a country's currency relative to another currency, group of currencies.

Sounds with frequencies higher than 20 kHz are called ultrasonic sound or ultrasound.

These sounds are beyond the audible range of humans but can be heard by certain animals like bats and dolphins.

The human hearing range is typically 20 Hz to 20 kHz (20,000 Hz).

Sonic refers to sound within the audible range (20 Hz to 20 kHz).

Supersonic relates to speeds faster than sound, not frequency. Ultrasonic sounds are used in applications like medical imaging (ultrasound), cleaning, and animal communication (e.g., bats use ultrasonic waves for echolocation).

Elements in the same group (vertical column) of the periodic table are defined by having the same number of valence electrons, which are the electrons in the outermost shell of an atom.

Explanation of Options:

Atomic number: This is incorrect. The atomic number (number of protons) increases as you move down a group. For example, in Group 1, Hydrogen has an atomic number of 1, Lithium has 3, and Sodium has 11.

Valence electrons: This is the correct answer. The number of valence electrons determines an element's chemical properties and bonding behavior. For example, all elements in Group 1 (the alkali metals) have 1 valence electron. All elements in Group 17 (the halogens) have 7 valence electrons. This similarity in valence electron configuration is the reason why elements in the same group exhibit similar chemical properties.

Atomic mass: This is incorrect. The atomic mass increases significantly as you move down a group, due to the addition of more protons and neutrons in the nucleus.

Electron affinity: This is incorrect. Electron affinity, the energy change when an electron is added to a neutral atom, generally decreases (becomes less negative) as you move down a group, although there are exceptions. It is not the same for all elements in a group.

Further insights:

The periodic table is a masterful organization of elements. Its structure allows us to predict the properties of elements based on their position. The group number itself often indicates the number of valence electrons for the main group elements (Groups 1-2 and 13-18). For example, elements in Group 14 (like Carbon and Silicon) have 4 valence electrons.

Arabian Sea: This is a branch of the main southwest monsoon.

Mediterranean Sea: This is the correct origin point. These low-pressure systems are carried towards India by subtropical westerly jet streams.

Indian Ocean: The Indian Ocean is the primary source of moisture for the main summer monsoon, not the winter disturbances in the north.

Further insights:

Western disturbances are crucial for the rabi crops, including wheat, which are grown in North India during the winter.

They are also responsible for the snowfall in the higher reaches of the Himalayas, which replenishes glaciers that feed the major North Indian rivers.

questions.solution:
Statements 1 and 2 are correct descriptions of officials within the Gupta administration.

Statement 3 is incorrect because while Mahamatyas were high officials, other specific officers were designated for land revenue collection during the Gupta period.

Explanation of Statements:

Statement 1 is correct. In the Gupta administration, the Sandhi-Vigrahika was the minister responsible for foreign affairs, specifically managing matters of peace ("Sandhi") and war ("Vigraha"). This role is famously associated with Harisena, the composer of the Allahabad Pillar Inscription, who served under Emperor Samudragupta.

Statement 2 is correct. The Kumaramatyas formed a key cadre of high-ranking imperial officers in the Gupta Empire. They functioned as an elite civil service and were appointed by the king to various important posts, including ministers, provincial governors, and district heads, playing a vital role in the administration of the empire.

Statement 3 is incorrect. The term Mahamatya was a general title for a high-ranking minister or official. However, the specific function of collecting the king's share of land revenue was carried out by officials known as Dhruvadhikaranas. The administration of land and revenue was overseen at the district level by the Vishayapati. Assigning the specific role of land revenue collection to the general title of Mahamatya is not accurate for the Gupta administrative system.

Further insights:

The Gupta administration was well-organized but more decentralized than the preceding Mauryan empire.

The empire was divided into provinces (Bhuktis), which were governed by Uparikas.

Provinces were subdivided into districts (Vishayas), administered by Vishayapatis.

This structured hierarchy of officials, from the central ministers like the Sandhi-Vigrahika down to the district and village levels, ensured the efficient governance of the vast Gupta empire.

India's innovation journey reached a new milestone in 2025 with the country rising to the 38th position in the Global Innovation Index (GII), assessed across 139 economies by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO).

India's strengths lie in its scale, entrepreneurial activity and a growing ability to translate scientific knowledge into commercial impact.

India stands out for its ICT services exports, a vibrant venture capital landscape, late-stage venture capital and startup financing, unicorns and intangible assets, reflecting tech-driven growth.

Over the past decade, India has steadily climbed from the 81st spot in 2015 to 48th in 2020, 40th by 2022, 39th in 2024, and now 38th in 2025. This trajectory demonstrates structural progress in building a dynamic innovation ecosystem.

India now stands as the top innovator among lower-middle-income economies and ranks first in Central & Southern Asia. The country's leadership is reflected in strong performance in critical innovation outputs: India ranks first in ICT services exports, fourth in late-stage venture capital deals, eighth in intangible asset intensity, and eleventh in unicorn valuations.

The Global Innovation Index (GII) ranks world economies according to their innovation capabilities. Consisting of roughly 80 indicators, grouped into innovation inputs and outputs, the GII aims to capture the multi-dimensional facets of innovation.

Further insights:

India has four clusters in the top 100: Bengaluru (21st), Delhi (26th), Mumbai (46th) and Chennai (84th), with most clusters boosted significantly by the inclusion of venture capital deal counts.

Switzerland, Sweden, USA, South Korea and Singapore top the Index, followed by the United Kingdom, Finland, Netherlands, Denmark and China, which breaks into the top 10 for the first time.

Phylum Mollusca is characterized by animals that have a soft, unsegmented body, which in many species is protected by a hard, calcareous shell.

Explanation of Options:

a) Echinodermata: This phylum includes animals like starfish, sea urchins, and sea cucumbers. They are characterized by a spiny skin and radial symmetry in adults, not a soft body with a shell.

b) Arthropoda: This is the largest phylum and includes insects, spiders, and crustaceans. Their defining features are a hard exoskeleton made of chitin and jointed appendages, not a soft body.

c) Mollusca: This is the correct answer. It is the second-largest phylum of invertebrate animals. The body plan generally includes a muscular foot for locomotion, a visceral mass containing the organs, and a mantle that often secretes a shell. Examples include snails, clams, oysters, and octopuses (which have lost their external shell through evolution).

d) Annelida: This phylum consists of segmented worms, such as earthworms and leeches. Their key characteristic is a body made up of a series of repeating segments. They are soft-bodied but do not have a shell.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The Active voice in this question is in Past Indefinite. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Past Indefinite.

The format of the active voice is: Subject + V2 + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Subject (a vase) + was/were + V3 + by + Object (him).

Option b) is eliminated as it uses the past perfect tense.

Option c) is eliminated as it is grammatically incorrect; it changes the tense of the second verb (fling) into simple present tense.

Option d) is eliminated as it uses the past continuous tense, while the original sentence uses the simple past tense.

Hence, option a) is correct.

The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

• The reporting verb 'said to' is changed into 'told'.

• 'I' is changed into 'she'.

• The verb 'am' is changed into 'was'.

• 'My' is changed into 'her,

Therefore, the correct answer is: The student told me that she was eager to learn and share her experience.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate tense form to fill in the blank. We ___ the concert together next weekend.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate tense form to fill in the blank.

We ___ the concert together next weekend.
questions.solution:
The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is 'will attend'. The sentence describes something that will happen in the future (next weekend). 'Will attend' is correct as it is in the simple future tense, indicating the planned attendance at the concert next weekend. Option (a) is grammatically incorrect. In the future tense, we use "will" with the base form of the verb, not with "s" at the end. Option (b) is incorrect. "Would" is used for conditional statements or polite requests, not for future tense statements. 'Would' does not indicate a definite future event. Also, it is not appropriate to use 'would' directly with 'attending'. 'Would be attending' is the appropriate expression. It indicates an ongoing or continuous action in the future. "Would" should be followed by "be" and the present participle form of the verb ("attending") to indicate an ongoing future action. Option (c) is incorrect. "Attended" is the past tense form of the verb "to attend", and it doesn't fit with the future tense context of the sentence. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

The complete sentence is: We will attend the concert together next weekend.

NOTE:

Participle: A word formed from a verb (e.g. going, gone, being, been) and used as an adjective (e.g. working woman, burnt toast) or a noun (e.g. good breeding). In English, participles are also used to make compound verb forms (e.g. is going, has been). Consider the sentences given below:

Dancing at the party, the woman fell on the ground.

Encouraged by her parents, Rita went on to pursue her passion.

The highlighted word in the first sentence is of the form Verb + ing and is used as a present participle. It is used to denote an action that is going on or incomplete or imperfect.

The highlighted word in the second sentence is of the form verb + ed. It is used as a past participle. It denotes the completed action or state of the thing spoken of.

A past participle ends with the following: -ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n.

One should take great care and never get confused between a gerund and a present participle. They use the same forms but perform different functions: a gerund is a verbal noun, while a present participle is a verbal adjective.

questions.question: Which among the following sentences uses the adjective with the correct degree of comparison?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following sentences uses the adjective with the correct degree of comparison?

options.text: This plan involves the littlest amount of work.

options.html: This plan involves the least amount of work.

options.text: This plan involves the less amount of work.
options.html: This plan involves the less amount of work.

options.text: This plan involves the most little amount of work.

questions.solution:
The adjective "little" has two irregular forms. When referring to size, the forms are "littler" and "littlest." When referring to quantity or amount (especially with uncountable nouns like "work"), the forms are "less" and "least."

· Option (a): Incorrect. "Littlest" refers to physical size, not quantity. "Amount" signals that we are talking about quantity, so "least" is the correct choice.

· Option (b): Correct. "Least" is the correct superlative form of "little" when referring to an amount.

· Option (c): Incorrect. "Less" is the comparative degree, but "amount" requires the superlative when comparing within a set. The correct phrase would have been "a lesser amount of work" in another context.

· Option (d): Incorrect. This is not the correct way to form the superlative of "little."

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note: · The Positive Degree is used to denote the mere existence of some quality of what we speak about. It is used when no comparison is made.

· The Comparative degree denotes a higher degree of quality than the positive and is used when two things are compared.

· The Superlative degree indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.
